name: Close
description: Sales CRM built for inside-sales teams with built-in calling, SMS, and email.
gating_notes: API keys are generated directly by any Close user from Settings → Developer → API Keys and used via HTTP Basic auth; Close offers a free trial, so developers can self-serve without a sales conversation. OAuth 2.0 is also available for user-facing integrations (requires creating an OAuth app).
mcp_notes: Official first-party Close MCP server at https://mcp.close.com/mcp, documented at developer.close.com/mcp/. Supports OAuth 2.0 Dynamic Client Registration (recommended) or API key via the Close-API-Key header, with a three-tier scope model — mcp.read, mcp.write_safe, mcp.write_destructive — set via the Close-Scope header or chosen at OAuth authorization; each tier unlocks a different tool set.

_critic.notes: The 404 was a false positive for the substance of the claim: the dead dev.to blog post was the only weak source, and every field it backed is confirmed by Close's own developer docs. developer.close.com/mcp/ documents an official first-party MCP server at https://mcp.close.com/mcp with exactly the three-tier scope model claimed (mcp.read / mcp.write_safe / mcp.write_destructive) and both OAuth 2.0 DCR and Close-API-Key auth; developer.close.com/topics/authentication/ confirms self-serve API key generation at Settings → Developer → API Keys plus OAuth. I replaced the dead link with the two official docs pages, firmed up mcp_notes from 'appears first-party' to confirmed, and raised confidence to high.
